subject: english
title: 九下 · 中考全范围早鸟卷 · 英语
source: 按中考英语题型、题量编写（不含听力），难度略高于中考，百分制
note: 51 题，不含听力，百分制，难度略高于中考

items.stem: —Have you ever been to ____ Great Wall? —Yes. It's ____ amazing place.
items.exp: the Great Wall 是固定说法；amazing 以元音音素开头，用 an。

items.stem: Neither my parents nor my brother ____ at home when I came back yesterday.
items.exp: neither...nor... 连接主语时，谓语与靠近的主语 my brother 一致，且时间是 yesterday，用 was。坑点：看到 parents 就用复数。

items.stem: The book is so interesting that I have read it ____ times.
items.exp: 表示“读了几遍”用基数词 two times（也可说 twice）。“a second time”表示“再一次”，与 have read it 后接次数不符。

items.stem: —Could you tell me ____? —Next Monday.
options: when will we visit the museum
when we will visit the museum
when did we visit the museum
items.exp: 宾语从句用陈述语序；答语 Next Monday 是将来，用一般将来时。

items.stem: My grandfather ____ in this small town since he retired ten years ago.
items.exp: since＋过去时间点，主句用现在完成时。

items.stem: You ____ be tired after such a long trip. Sit down and have a rest.
items.exp: 肯定推测“一定”用 must；can't 表示否定推测“不可能”。

items.stem: The new bridge ____ next year. It will make traveling much easier.
items.exp: 桥是“被建造”，时间 next year，用一般将来时的被动语态。

items.stem: This is the village ____ I lived when I was a child.
items.exp: 先行词 village 在从句中作地点状语（lived in the village），用 where。坑点：live 是不及物动词，不能直接用 which/that。

items.stem: —I failed the math test again. I'm not good at it at all. —____ Practice makes perfect.
items.exp: 对方灰心，后文 Practice makes perfect，应鼓励“别放弃”。

items.stem: It was ____ heavy rain that the sports meeting had to be put off.
items.exp: rain 在这里是不可数名词，用 such＋形容词＋不可数名词。坑点：rain 不可数，不能加 a。

sections.title: A Note on the Desk
sections.passage:
Last winter, I was preparing for an important piano competition. Every day after school, I practiced for two hours, but one piece always (11) me. My fingers seemed to get lost in the fast part, and I made the same mistake again and again.
One evening, I was so (12) that I hit the keys hard and shouted, "I'll never play it well!" Then I ran into my room and closed the door.
The next morning, I found a note on my desk. It was from my grandma, who lived with us. She had (13) learned to play the piano, but she listened to me every day. The note said, "Yesterday you played the first part (14) than last week. I heard it. Did you?"
I read it twice. I had only noticed my mistakes. I had never (15) the progress I had made.
That afternoon, I didn't practice the whole piece at once. (16), I played the fast part very slowly, one small bar at a time. When I could play a bar (17) any mistakes three times, I moved to the next one. It was boring, but it (18).
On the day of the competition, my hands were shaking. I looked at the audience and saw Grandma sitting in the front row, smiling. I took a deep breath and began. When I reached the fast part, my fingers knew (19) to go.
I didn't win first prize, but I won something more important. Now, whenever I feel like giving up, I remember Grandma's note: the progress you don't notice is still (20).

items.exp: 下文总在快的部分出错，说明这首曲子一直困扰着“我”。
重重地敲琴键、大喊“永远弹不好”，说明心烦意乱。
but she listened to me every day 构成转折：她从没学过钢琴，却每天听“我”弹。
下文说“我”只注意到错误，从没注意到进步，奶奶指出的是“比上周弹得更好”。坑点：faster 不能体现“进步”。
与上一句 only noticed my mistakes 对应：从没注意到自己的进步。
不一次弹整首，“而是”一小节一小节地慢慢弹，用 Instead。
能“不出错地”连弹三遍才进入下一节。
虽然枯燥，但很有效（work 表示“起作用”），与下文比赛中手指“知道往哪走”呼应。
my fingers knew where to go：手指知道该往哪里去，与开头 fingers seemed to get lost 呼应。
结尾点题：你没注意到的进步，依然是进步。

groups.label: A
groups.title: Weekend Courses at Greenfield Youth Center
groups.passage:
Weekend Courses at Greenfield Youth Center (March 1 – May 31)
First Aid Basics — Saturdays 9:00–11:00. Learn how to deal with small cuts, burns and nosebleeds. Ages 12–16. Fee: ¥60 for 4 lessons. Each student gets a free first-aid kit.
Photography for Beginners — Saturdays 14:00–16:00. Bring your own phone or camera. Ages 10 and up. Fee: ¥120 for 6 lessons. The best photos will be shown in our hall in June.
Cooking for Teens — Sundays 10:00–12:00. Make simple, healthy meals for your family. Ages 13–17. Fee: ¥150 for 5 lessons (food included).
Robot Club — Sundays 15:00–17:00. Build and program small robots in teams of three. Ages 11–15. Fee: ¥200 for 8 lessons. No experience needed.
Notes: Students who sign up for two courses get 20% off the second one (the cheaper one). Sign up at the front desk or call 6688-3721 before February 25.

items.stem: Which course offers something free to every student?
items.exp: First Aid Basics：Each student gets a free first-aid kit。

items.stem: Tom is 16 and is free only on Sunday mornings. Which course can he take?
items.exp: 周日上午只有 Cooking for Teens（10:00–12:00），且 13–17 岁，16 岁符合。Robot Club 在周日下午且只到 15 岁。

items.stem: Lily, 14, signs up for Photography and Robot Club. How much should she pay in all?
items.exp: 第二门（较便宜的一门）打八折：摄影 120×80%＝96，机器人 200，共 296 元。坑点：打折的是较便宜的那门，不是较贵的。

items.stem: What can we learn from the passage?
options: All the courses are for students over 12.
Students must sign up before March 1.
Photos from the photography course may be shown in June.
Students need experience to join the Robot Club.
items.exp: The best photos will be shown in our hall in June。报名截止是 February 25；摄影课 10 岁以上即可；机器人社 No experience needed。

items.stem: Where is the passage most probably from?
items.exp: 列出课程时间、费用和报名方式，是海报或广告。

groups.label: B
groups.title: The Boy Who Fixed Bikes
groups.passage:
Fourteen-year-old Chen Hao lives in a small town where many people ride bikes to work and school. Two years ago, his own bike broke down on the way to school, and he had to walk for forty minutes. "I was late for the first time in my life," he said. "I decided I would learn to fix bikes myself."
He watched online videos and practiced on old bikes his neighbors no longer wanted. At first, he made a lot of mistakes. Once, he put a chain back the wrong way, and the bike made a terrible noise. But he didn't give up. He wrote down every mistake in a notebook and checked it before each repair.
Soon, classmates began to ask him for help. Chen Hao set up a "Saturday Bike Corner" outside the community center. He fixes bikes there for free, but asks each person to do one small thing in return: help another person in the town. "Some people help old people carry things, and some clean the park," he said. "Kindness travels like a bike — it keeps moving if you keep pushing."
Last month, the town gave him an award. The money from the award was used to buy tools and a small shed for the Bike Corner. Now, five other students work with him every Saturday. "I used to think I was just fixing bikes," Chen Hao said. "Now I know I'm helping people get to where they want to go."

items.stem: Why did Chen Hao decide to learn to fix bikes?
options: Because he wanted to win an award.
Because he was late for school when his bike broke.
Because his neighbors asked him to.
Because he wanted to make money.
items.exp: 第一段：自行车坏在上学路上，走了 40 分钟，第一次迟到，于是决定学修车。

items.stem: What did Chen Hao do to avoid making the same mistakes?
options: He kept a notebook of his mistakes.
He asked his classmates for help.
items.exp: He wrote down every mistake in a notebook and checked it before each repair.

items.stem: What does Chen Hao ask people to do in return?
options: Pay a small amount of money.
Help someone else in the town.
items.exp: asks each person to do one small thing in return: help another person in the town。清理公园只是例子之一。

items.stem: What does the underlined sentence "Kindness travels like a bike — it keeps moving if you keep pushing" mean?
options: Riding bikes is a kind thing to do.
Kindness can spread if people keep passing it on.
People should push their bikes instead of riding them.
Kindness is as fast as a bike.
items.exp: 把善意比作骑车：只要大家不断“往前推”（传递下去），善意就会一直传下去。

items.stem: Which of the following best describes Chen Hao?
items.exp: 犯错不放弃（determined），免费修车并鼓励人们互相帮助（caring）。

groups.label: C
groups.title: Why We Forget
groups.passage:
Have you ever studied hard for a test, only to forget most of it a week later? You are not alone. More than a hundred years ago, a German scientist named Hermann Ebbinghaus studied how people forget. He found that we forget new information very quickly at first, and then more slowly. Without review, a large part of what we learn today may be gone within a day or two.
The good news is that forgetting can be slowed down. Ebbinghaus discovered that each time we review something, we forget it more slowly than before. This idea led to a learning method called "spaced repetition". Instead of studying something many times in one night, you review it after one day, then after three days, then after a week, and so on. Each review comes just before you are about to forget.
Why does this work? When we try to remember something that is a little difficult to recall, our brain works harder, and the memory becomes stronger. In contrast, reading the same page again and again in one evening feels easy, but the feeling of "I know this" can be misleading. The information is in our short-term memory, not our long-term memory.
Many students now use apps or simple notebooks to plan their reviews. Some write each new word on a card and move the card to a different box each time they remember it correctly. The cards they keep forgetting stay in the first box and come up more often.
Of course, spaced repetition is not magic. It works best for facts, words and formulas. To understand difficult ideas, you still need to think, ask questions and practice. But if you want to remember what you learn, it may be time to stop cramming and start spacing.

items.stem: According to Ebbinghaus, how do people forget new information?
options: Quickly at first, then more slowly.
At the same speed all the time.
items.exp: 第一段：we forget new information very quickly at first, and then more slowly。

items.stem: Which plan follows the idea of spaced repetition?
options: Reading a lesson five times on Sunday night.
Reviewing a lesson after 1 day, 3 days and 7 days.
Reviewing a lesson only before the test.
Copying a lesson ten times in one hour.
items.exp: 间隔重复是隔 1 天、3 天、一周依次复习。

items.stem: Why can reading the same page again and again in one evening be misleading?
options: Because it makes us feel tired.
Because the information is only in short-term memory.
Because the page is too difficult.
Because our brain works too hard.
items.exp: 第三段：重复读感觉很容易，但信息只在短期记忆里，“我会了”的感觉会误导人。

items.stem: What does the word "cramming" in the last paragraph probably mean?
options: Studying a lot in a short time just before a test.
items.exp: 与 spacing（分散复习）相对，指考前短时间内突击塞进大量内容（临时抱佛脚）。

items.stem: What is the writer's attitude towards spaced repetition?
options: It can solve all learning problems.
It is useful for remembering, but not enough for understanding.
It is only useful for scientists.
It is not as good as reading many times.
items.exp: 最后一段：间隔重复不是魔法，适合记忆事实、单词和公式；理解难点还需思考、提问和练习。

sections.title: How to Make a Study Plan That Works
sections.passage:
Many students make study plans at the beginning of a term, but few of them follow the plans for more than two weeks. (36) Here are some tips.
Be realistic. A plan that asks you to study six hours every day after school is hard to keep. Start with what you can really do. (37)
Break big tasks into small ones. "Review Chapter 3" sounds simple, but it may take hours. (38) Small tasks are easier to start and give you a sense of success when you finish them.
Leave some free time. Life is full of surprises: a friend's birthday, a cold, extra homework. (39) If nothing happens, you can use that time to rest or catch up.
Check and change your plan. At the end of each week, look at what you have finished. (40) Maybe some subjects need more time, or maybe you work better in the morning. A good plan is not one you never change, but one that keeps getting better.
choices: So how can we make a plan we can actually follow?
Don't fill every minute of your plan with study.
You can always add more later.
Ask yourself what worked and what didn't.
Good students never need study plans.
Studying late at night is the best way to learn.

items.exp: 下一句 Here are some tips，空处应提出问题：怎样制订能坚持下去的计划。
先从能做到的开始，“以后随时可以再加”。
上一句说“复习第三章”太笼统，用 Instead 给出具体小任务的写法。
本段主题是“留出空闲时间”，生活中有意外，所以不要把每一分钟都排满。
每周检查完成情况，问自己哪些有效、哪些无效，下文接着说可能哪些科目需要更多时间。

sections.title: My First Speech
sections.passage:
I used to be very shy. In class, I seldom (41) (raise) my hand, even when I knew the answer. Last term, our English teacher asked each of us to give a three-minute speech. When I heard the news, I felt (42) (terrible) nervous.
To prepare, I wrote my speech and practiced it in front of the mirror (43) (many) times than I can remember. My mother listened to me every evening and gave me (44) (suggest). "Speak slowly and look at your listeners," she said.
On the day of the speech, I was the (45) (one) to speak. My heart was beating fast. But when I saw my best friend (46) (smile) at me, I felt much better. I took a deep breath and began. To my surprise, the words came out (47) (easy).
When I finished, everyone clapped. My teacher said it was one of the (48) (good) speeches she had heard that term. I was so happy that I couldn't stop smiling.
From this experience, I learned that we can't become brave without (49) (try). Now I am no longer afraid of speaking in public. I believe that I can do (50) (I) best if I am well prepared.

items.exp: used to be 描述过去，句子叙述过去的情况，用 raised。
修饰形容词 nervous 用副词 terribly。
后有 than，用比较级 more。
give sb. suggestions，suggestion 可数，每天都给建议用复数。
the first to do 第一个做某事的人。
see sb. doing 表示看到某人正在做某事；see sb. do 也可接受。
修饰动词 came out 用副词 easily。
one of the＋最高级＋复数名词。
介词 without 后用动名词 trying。
do one's best，主语是 I，用 my。

sections.prompt:
初三学习任务重，很多同学感到压力大。你校英语报正在开展以“How I Deal with Stress”为题的征文活动。请写一篇短文，内容包括：1. 你感到压力的一个具体情况；2. 你是怎样应对的（至少两种方法）；3. 效果如何；4. 给同学的一条建议。要求：90—110 词，开头已给出，不计入总词数；文中不得出现真实姓名和校名。
How I Deal with Stress
In Grade 9, almost everyone feels stressed sometimes. ______
points: 写清一个具体的压力情境
至少写出两种应对方法，并说明具体做法
写出效果，并给同学一条建议
语言准确，句式有变化，衔接自然，书写规范
sections.sample:
How I Deal with Stress
In Grade 9, almost everyone feels stressed sometimes. Last month, I did badly in a math test, and I worried that I would never catch up.
To deal with it, I first talked with my parents. They listened patiently and told me one test couldn't decide everything. Then I made a simple plan. Every evening, I spent twenty minutes going over my mistakes instead of doing piles of new exercises. I also went jogging three times a week, which helped me relax.
Two weeks later, I felt much calmer, and my next test result was better.
My advice is: don't keep stress to yourself. Talk to someone and take one small step at a time.
sections.exp: 评分时先看要点是否齐全，再看语言。高分句型：instead of doing、which 引导的非限制性定语从句、... helped me do sth.。
